messages.subject: stan and machine learning
parts:
Hi,

Has anybody used stan for machine learning applications?  The problem is to figure out what is a regular commercial flight and what is a diversion.  I have a model for regular commercial flights but have no clue how to model diversions.

Attached are the histogram of passenger number data and a fit of data using the model for regular commercial flights.  In the histogram one can easily see two peaks - regular commercial flights on the right and diversions on the left.  Fit shows existence of at least two clusters.  Any suggestions how to "filter" out the diversion data?  I was thinking about a mixture of two Poissons, one for regular flights using the regular flight model and one just random Poisson noise for diversions but I hope there are better approaches.

Thanks a lot,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan and machine learning
parts:
If you build the model as a mixture, you can
calculate posterior probabilities for each mixture
component on a per-item basis. That is, you get a
probabilistic classifier for free. Is it the
classification aspect of this that you think of as
machine learning?

If there are covariates, the Poissons can have means
estimated by a GLM.

And there's almost always overdispersion in real data,
so you might want to try negative binomial instead (just
be careful about all the parameterizations floating around
the literature and in Stan).

- Bob
